name: Sikadur-42 HF
paste:
SIKADUR®-42 HF: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-42 HF, February 2025, Version 03.05 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/5/sikadur-42-hf.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-42 HF where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (February 2025, Version 03.05).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur®-42 HF is a pourable, multi-functional high density epoxy grout based on a 2-component solvent free epoxy resin system containing fine fillers. Sikadur®-42 HF exhibits excellent insolubility and displacement characteristics in wet and underwater applications but useable in dry general grouting applications also.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur®-42 HF may only be used by experienced professionals. As a grout for manufacturing plants and civil engineering application:
    - Crane rails
    - Machine bedding and baseplates
    - Holding down bolts
    - Stanchions
    - Starter bars
    - Cavity filling
    - Bridge bearings
    Sikadur®-42 HF may be used for underwater work and offers excellent adhesion to both dry and clean water immersed concrete, stone masonry, brick, wood or steel surfaces. Highly insoluble in water and safe for specialist diver use. Used for injection of cracks 0.5mm to 40mm wide under water (cracks not conducting a water flow under pressure). Ideal for pile jacketing using prepacked aggregate in formwork. Mixed with 30% by volume sand a high build grout is formed that is easy to apply under water. May also be used as a bonding bridge for underwater concreting and as a pipeline jointing material.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-42 HF
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Very High Flow, Water Displacing, Cost Effective Epoxy Resin Grout
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 1504-4 - Structural bonding
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 1504-5 - Concrete Injection
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 1504-6 - Anchoring of reinforcing steel bar
    - ASTM D3755-20 Dielectric Breakdown Voltage and Dielectric Strength of Solid Electrical Insulating Materials Under Direct-Voltage Stress
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-4: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 1504-5: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 1504-6: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - ASTM D3755-20: listed under approvals, certificates or standards; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1); Product Information > Electrical resistivity (p.2).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - ASTM C 348: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Flexural-strength (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Cost effective epoxy grout.
    - Suitable for dry, wet, underwater or marine applications.
    - Highly insoluble in water and suitable for application by specialist divers.
    - Applicable at low temperatures.
    - High mechanical strengths.
    - High flow characteristics.
    - Supplied in factory proportioned units.
    - Shrink free.
    - Can be bulked out with aggregate of thicker pour applications.
    - Excellent chemical resistance to water, sea water, waste water.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Density: 2.0 kg / litre approx.
    - Viscosity: 2,500 to 3,000 mPa.s approx. (+23oC)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore D Hardness: 81 approx. (10 days at +20 oC)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: Dynamic 7,800 MPa approx. Static 6,300 MPa approx. (14 days at 20 oC)
    - Flexural-strength: ~ 35 MPa (14 days) (ASTM C 348)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 25 MPa (+20 oC approx.) (DIN 42 HF455)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: 10 to 13 MPa (on steel); 2.5 to 3.5 MPa (concrete failure) (EN 1542)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: ~ 7.5 × 10–5 1/K (Temp. range -20 °C – +60 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Electrical resistivity: Dielectric Breakdown Voltage & Strength; > 30.0 kV/mm (ASTM D3755-20)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | 24 hrs | ~ 50 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 88 MPa |
    | 14 days | ~ 90 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
    Note printed: Test specimen cured and tested at +23 oC / 50% r.h. and 50mm cube size.
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 18 kg net pre-proportioned kit
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Stored properly in original and unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sun light.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (February 2025, Version 03.05) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - Mortar and concrete must be older than 28 days (dependent on minimum strength requirements). Verify the substrate strength (concrete, natural stone etc.). The substrate surface (all types) must be clean, dry and free from contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, existing surface treatments and coatings etc. Steel substrates must be de-rusted to a standard equivalent to Sa 2.5.
    - The substrate must be sound and all loose particles must be removed. Substrate must be dry or mat damp and free from any standing water, ice etc.
3.3 Substrate preparation. Surface and base plate contact area must be clean and sound. For best results, the substrate should be dry. Remove dust, laitance, oils, grease, curing compounds, impregnations, waxes, foreign particles, coatings, and disintegrated materials by mechanical means, i.e. chipping with a chisel, blastcleaning etc. All anchor pockets or sleeves must be free of water. Blastcleaning metal base plates to an acceptable quality standard equivalent to SA 2.5 for maximum adhesion. Apply grout immediately to prevent re-oxidizing.
3.4 Substrate preparation - Forming. The consistency of the Sikadur®-42 HF epoxy grout system requires the use of permanent or temporary forms to contain the material around base plates, for example. In order to prevent leakage or seepage, all of these formers must be sealed. Apply polyethylene film or wax to all forms to prevent adhesion of the grout. Prepare the formwork to maintain more than 100 mm liquid head to facilitate placement. A grout box equipped with an inclined trough attached to the form will enhance the grout flow and minimize air encapsulation.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (February 2025, Version 03.05) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: A : B = 8 : 1 by weight; A : B = 3.6 : 1 by volume
    - Consumption: 2.0 kg/m2 approx. per mm thickness
    - Yield: 18 kg kit yields approximately 9 litres of grout
    - Layer thickness: 0.50 mm min. / 40 mm max.
    - Curing time: 24 hours (+20 oC)
4.3 Pot Life. 50 minutes approx. @ 20 °C for 1.8 kg mix; 35 minutes approx. @ 20 °C for 18 kg mix; (The temperature at which the Sikadur-42 HF is stored during the 24 hours before it is mixed will govern its potlife when mixed).
4.4 Mixing.
    - Prior to mixing the components should be stored at 15-20°C for the previous 24 hours. Mix all of component A (Grey Resin) with all of component B (Hardener) using a slow speed drill (maximum 600 rpm) and windmill stirrer. Mix until a homogeneous and streak free mixture results.
    - If placing underwater allow to stand for 10-15 minutes after mixing before placing.
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - Mixed Sikadur®-42 HF should be poured into the void or formwork from one side to avoid the entrapment of air. Continuous grout flow is essential and there must be sufficient grout available before pouring.
    - Machine Base Plates & Crane Rails: An adequate head must be maintained to ensure continuous flow. Continue pouring until the grout rises above the level of the plate. At no time during application should the grout head be less than 50 mm above the level of the plate. This, as well as adequate vent holes, is essential to ensure no air is trapped.
    - Anchor Bolts and Dowels: For bolts placed into preformed holes, fill the hole with Sikadur®-42 HF and place into the grout.
    - Higher strengths achieved if placed using a tremmie placing technique rather than free fall through water. When using Sikadur®-42 HF as a bonding bridge the material may be applied by brush or gloved hand. Ensure an even continuous film. Place fresh concrete immediately.
    - If injecting cracks, pressure equipment may be used (eg. liquid tight bulk sealant gun; hand pumped grease filling equipment and high pressure pumping equipment may also be used).
    - Large voids may be filled by pre-filling with clean aggregate.
    - Where possible use coarse rounded river gravel not smaller than 8mm and pouring or injecting/ tremmieing Sikadur®-42 HF into the void, displacing the water (i.e. preplaced aggregate technique).
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Sweep excess grout into appropriate containers for disposal before it has hardened. Dispose of in accordance with applicable local regulations. Uncured material can be removed with Sika Colma Cleaner. Cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not part mix kits.
    - Only mix as many kits as can be applied within the stated potlife.
    - Do not dilute the product with solvent as this will affect both the cure and in-service performance of the product.
    - Minimum thickness 0.5mm, maximum thickness 40mm.
    - The temperature at which the Sikadur®-42 HF is stored during the 24 hours before it is mixed will govern its potlife when mixed.
    - Minimum age of new concrete, 4 to 6 weeks.
    - Sikadur®-42 HF will rise in temperature when mixing. The extent of this temperature rise will depend upon the volume to surface ratio and the ambient and substrate temperature.
    - Refer to the Sikadur 42 Method statement for guidence in correct methods for epoxy grouting applications.
    - Do not apply under water at depths greater than 5m without referral to our Technical Department.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. 5 oC min. / 35 oC max.
5.3 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.7):
    - The temperature at which the Sikadur®-42 HF is stored during the 24 hours before it is mixed will govern its potlife when mixed.
    - Sikadur®-42 HF will rise in temperature when mixing. The extent of this temperature rise will depend upon the volume to surface ratio and the ambient and substrate temperature.
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: 24 hrs | ~ 50 MPa; 7 days | ~ 88 MPa; 14 days | ~ 90 MPa (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Flexural-strength: ~ 35 MPa (14 days) (ASTM C 348)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 25 MPa (+20 oC approx.) (DIN 42 HF455)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: 10 to 13 MPa (on steel); 2.5 to 3.5 MPa (concrete failure) (EN 1542)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: ~ 7.5 × 10–5 1/K (Temp. range -20 °C – +60 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Electrical resistivity: Dielectric Breakdown Voltage & Strength; > 30.0 kV/mm (ASTM D3755-20)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-42 HF, February 2025, Version 03.05, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/5/sikadur-42-hf.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur 42HF Part A, version 21/11/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/l/Sikadur%2042HF%20Part%20A-GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur 42HF Part B, version 21/11/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/Sikadur%2042HF%20Part%20B.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-42 HF Part A, version 30/01/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/l/sds-sikadur-42-hfparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
